newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Nov 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Nov 7.

text.p: Combined capital investment by cellular phone companies, including NTT Mobile Communications Network Inc (NTT Do Co Mo), is expected to surge 98 percent to 1.47 trillion yen this business year to March, 1997 against a year earlier. The firms were initially expected to invest 1.28 trillion yen. The increase is due to strong sales of cellular phones.

The Finance Ministry is considering drafting legislation to protect individual investors against bankruptcies of securities houses. It plans to ask securities firms to contribute to public funds which would cover part of clients' losses if a securities firm goes bankrupt. It hopes to start the plan by April 1998.

Tokuyama Corp is expected to have increased its parent current profit by 75 percent to 4.2 billion yen in the half-year to September 30 compared with a year ago. It was helped by strong sales of polycrystalline silicon and cement.
Nisshin Steel Co Ltd plans to spend 20 billion yen to build a steel sheet galvanisation plant in Ehime Prefecture. It hopes to start operation in fiscal 1999/2000.

Domestic sales by Japanese carmakers of vehicles manufactured overseas are expected to drop in this calendar year. The car sales will be about 69,000 units in the January to October period, a drop of about 15 percent from the same period a year earlier, depressed by the weaker yen and a fall in new vehicle production.
Kyocera Corp is developing digital cellular phones based on the U.S. and European standards. It hopes to sell the phones in the United States, South America and Asian countries.
